violin.definition: Bowed stringed instrument that is the highest member of the violin family.
violin.exampleUsage: The violin was used during the activity.

viola.definition: Any of the numerous plants of the genus Viola.

cello.exampleUsage: The cello was used during the activity.

double-bass.definition: The largest and lowest-pitched common member of the orchestral string family.
double-bass.exampleUsage: The double bass played the lowest notes in the string section.

harp.definition: A large string instrument played by plucking its strings.

guitar.definition: A stringed instrument usually having six strings.
guitar.exampleUsage: The guitar was used during the activity.

bow.definition: An appearance by actors or performers at the end of the concert or play in order to acknowledge the applause of the audience.

string.definition: Stringed instruments that are played with a bow.
string.exampleUsage: The string was used during the activity.

tuning-peg.definition: A small peg or mechanism turned to adjust the tension and pitch of a musical instrument string.
tuning-peg.exampleUsage: The musician adjusted the tuning peg before rehearsal.

chin-rest.definition: A fitted support that lets a violinist rest the chin while holding and playing the instrument.
chin-rest.exampleUsage: The chin rest was used during the activity.

flute.exampleUsage: The flute was used during the activity.

clarinet.definition: A single-reed instrument with a straight tube.
clarinet.exampleUsage: The clarinet was used during the activity.

oboe.exampleUsage: The oboe was used during the activity.

bassoon.definition: A long, low-pitched woodwind instrument played with a double reed.

piccolo.definition: A small flute that makes very high notes.

recorder.definition: A tubular wind instrument with 8 finger holes and a fipple mouthpiece.
recorder.exampleUsage: The recorder was used during the activity.

saxophone.definition: A single-reed woodwind with a conical bore.

reed.definition: A vibrator consisting of a thin strip of stiff material that vibrates to produce a tone when air streams over it.

mouthpiece.definition: A part that goes over or into the mouth of a person.

key.definition: (basketball) a space (including the foul line) in front of the basket at each end of a basketball court.

trumpet.definition: A brass musical instrument with a brilliant tone.
trumpet.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Trumpet" in an educational description.

trombone.definition: A brass instrument consisting of a long tube whose length can be varied by a U-shaped slide.
trombone.exampleUsage: The trombone was used during the activity.

french-horn.definition: A brass instrument has a gradually widening tube wound into a spiral, with valves that alter the notes.
french-horn.exampleUsage: The french horn was used during the activity.

tuba.exampleUsage: The tuba was used during the activity.

cornet.definition: A brass musical instrument with a brilliant tone.
cornet.exampleUsage: The cornet was used during the activity.

bugle.definition: A simple brass instrument often used to play military calls.

valve.definition: A structure in a hollow organ (like the heart) with a flap to insure one-way flow of fluid through it.

bell.definition: A device that makes a ringing sound.
bell.exampleUsage: The bell was used during the activity.

mute.definition: To turn off or reduce sound from a microphone or instrument.

slide.definition: A smooth surface children slide down for fun.

drum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Drum" in an educational description.
drum.definition: A percussion instrument played by striking a stretched surface.

snare-drum.definition: A shallow drum has tightly stretched heads and wires held against the lower head. Striking it produces a sharp, rattling sound.
snare-drum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Snare Drum" in an educational description.

bass-drum.definition: A large percussion instrument with two heads produces a deep, indefinite-pitched sound.
bass-drum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Bass Drum" in an educational description.

timpani.definition: A large hemispherical brass or copper percussion instrument with a drumhead that can be tuned by adjusting the tension on it.
timpani.exampleUsage: The timpani was used during the activity.

cymbal.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a concave brass disk.
cymbal.exampleUsage: The cymbal was used during the activity.

triangle.definition: Something approximating the shape of a triangle.

xylophone.definition: A percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators.
xylophone.exampleUsage: The xylophone was used during the activity.

tambourine.definition: A shallow drum with a single drumhead and with metallic disks in the sides.

gong.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal plate that is struck with a softheaded drumstick.
gong.exampleUsage: The gong was used during the activity.

drumstick.definition: A stick used for playing a drum.
drumstick.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Drumstick" in an educational description.

concert-hall.definition: The professional and social world surrounding formal live music, from venue design and concert planning to audience traditions.

stage.definition: A large platform on which people can stand and can be seen by an audience.

music-stand.definition: A lightweight support keeps pages of written music open and visible while someone plays.

conductor-s-podium.definition: A small raised platform on which an orchestra conductor stands so musicians can see the conducting gestures.
conductor-s-podium.exampleUsage: The conductor stepped onto the podium.

baton.definition: A thin tapered rod used by a conductor to lead an orchestra or choir.

sheet-music.definition: A visual record of a musical work shows performers its notes, rhythms, volume changes, and other instructions.

score.definition: A number or letter indicating quality (especially of a student's performance).

tuning-fork.definition: A metal tool with two prongs produces a steady pitch when struck and helps musicians tune their instruments.
tuning-fork.exampleUsage: The tuning fork was used during the activity.

metronome.definition: Clicking pendulum indicates the exact tempo of a piece of music.

orchestra-pit.definition: A recessed area before a stage where musicians play while performers act or sing.

conductor.definition: The person who leads a musical group.

concertmaster.definition: A principal violinist leads the first violin section, connects the players with the conductor, tunes the orchestra, and coordinates bowing, phrasing, and cues.

soloist.definition: A musician who performs a solo.

first-chair.definition: The leading player in a section of an orchestra, usually seated closest to the conductor.
first-chair.exampleUsage: The first-chair violinist led the section.

section-leader.definition: The principal musician responsible for leading a particular instrumental section.
section-leader.exampleUsage: The section leader demonstrated the bowing pattern.

accompanist.definition: A person who provides musical accompaniment (usually on a piano).

composer.definition: A person who composes music, usually as a profession.

arranger.definition: A person who brings order and organization to an enterprise.

page-turner.definition: A person who turns the pages of printed music for a performer whose hands are occupied playing.
page-turner.exampleUsage: The page turner sat beside the pianist.

audience.definition: A gathering of spectators or listeners at a (usually public) performance.

podium.definition: A platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it.

symphony.definition: A long and complex sonata for symphony orchestra.

rehearsal.definition: A practice session in preparation for a public performance (as of a play or speech or concert).

program.definition: A system of projects or services intended to meet a public need.
